html:
The Soviet zone was the part of defeated Germany that the Soviet Union occupied from 1945 to 1949, covering the east of the country around Berlin, Saxony, Thuringia, Brandenburg and Mecklenburg. Berlin itself, inside the zone, was split among the four Allies.

The zones were agreed at the Yalta conference and the Potsdam Conference in 1945, after the defeat of Hitler in the Second World War. The Soviets took heavy reparations, dismantling whole factories and shipping them east. They broke up the big estates in a land reform, and in 1946 forced the Social Democrats to merge with the Communists into the Socialist Unity Party, which came to run everything. Millions of Germans expelled from the lost eastern lands arrived in the zone.

As the Cold War set in, Stalin tried to force the Western Allies out of Berlin with the Berlin Blockade of 1948 and 1949, and failed. In October 1949 the zone became the German Democratic Republic, East Germany.
